headline: Amended trash collection ordinance, approved preservation restrictions for two historic properties, denied Rackliffe Street fire lanes, and reduced early voting hours.
summary: The Council approved several parking and traffic ordinance changes, including new truck parking rules for Washington Square and a loading zone update on Main Street, but voted down adding fire lanes on Rackliffe Street after a lengthy debate. It approved preservation restrictions for the Haskell House and the Temple-Hayden Cottage, a National Grid utility pole on Bellevue Avenue, and changes to the City's trash and recycling ordinance. The Council also voted to reduce Early Voting hours for the first week before the November 3, 2026 State Election.
decisions: Appointed Philip Schwarz to the Open Space & Recreation Advisory Committee, term to expire 2/15/2027, 7-0.
Referred a $12,000 Wayfinding Signs Project funding request to the Budget & Finance Committee.
Approved payment of $51,317.23 in prior year invoices to the School Department, 7-0.
Approved payment of $440.94 to West Marine Pro for Police Department marine equipment, 7-0.
Accepted a FY2027 State 911 Emergency Medical Dispatch Grant of $42,528.96, 7-0.
Approved a National Grid permit to install a new utility pole at 17 Conant Avenue near Bellevue Avenue, 7-0.
Approved a preservation restriction agreement for the Haskell House at 11 Lincoln Street, 7-0.
Approved a preservation restriction agreement for the Temple-Hayden Cottage and Barn at 62-66 Eastern Point Boulevard, 7-0.
Accepted the withdrawal of the Special Council Permit application by 187 Atlantic Ave Holdings, LLC, without prejudice.
Amended Chapter 9 of the Gloucester Code of Ordinances governing trash, recycling, and litter, 7-0, including requiring private trash collection for buildings with five or more units.
Amended Chapter 22 to restrict commercial truck parking on Washington Square from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m., 7-0.
Failed, 0-7, a motion to add fire lanes on both sides of Rackliffe Street from Fremont Street to the dead end.
Continued a proposed no-parking/tow-away ordinance for Wheeler Street to the December 8, 2026 meeting.
Amended the Main Street service/loading zone ordinance to relocate and restrict a commercial loading space in front of #124, 7-0.
Amended the ordinance to delete a 30-minute parking zone on Eastern Avenue in front of #18, 7-0.
Amended parking restrictions on Rogers Street near Gorton's Seafood at 127 and 128 Rogers Street, removing four parking spaces, 7-0.
Approved reducing Early Voting hours for the first week of Early Voting for the November 3, 2026 State Election, 6-1.

of the agreement, as it is in the public’s interest to preserve this historic resource.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor Benson, the

the Preservation Restriction Agreement as defined in G.L. c. 184, secs. 31, 32, and 33 between the Society for the
Preservation of New England Antiquities dba Historic New England and a private purchaser to be identified at
the time of execution preserving the properties located at 62, 62R, 64, and 66 Eastern point Boulevard, Gloucester,
Map 135, Lots 20, 21, 22, and 23, specifically a portion of the site and the buildings known as the Temple-Hayden
Cottage and the Barn, as described in Exhibit A of the agreement, as it is in the public’s interest to preserve this
historic resource.
Summary of Discussion: Elizabeth Paliga stated that the Temple-Hayden Cottage had been erected in 1924,
after the owners had moved the circa 1750 Stowbridge House from Canton. She stated that the cottage was
significant for its origins as an 18th Century half-house but also its association with the development of Eastern
Point. She stated that Ruth Anderson was an acclaimed painter and studied under Eastern Point resident Cecilia
Beaux, and Samuel Temple, was a well-known lighting designer. She stated that the Hayden family had owned
the property from 1944 to 2020, when they sold the property to Historic New England, as development would
negatively impact the neighborhood and the adjacent Historic New England property of Beauport. She stated that
Historic New England had decided to sell the property into private ownership with a preservation restriction in
place. She stated that only the exterior would be protected by the restrictions, and interior alterations and upgrades
would be allowed.
MOTION: On a motion by Councilor Benson, seconded by Councilor Kimberley, the City Council voted

1. Memorandum from the City Clerk requesting to reduce Early Voting hours for the 1st week of Early
Voting for the November 3, 2026 State Election
Summary of Discussion: City Clerk, Grace Poirier stated that the State allows the Early Voting period to be
reduced by 50% with a vote by City Council. She stated that reducing the hours for the first week of Early Voting
would decrease the burden on staff, and makes the office able to concentrate on the high volume of vote-by-mail.
She stated that in the 2024 election there were only 77 in person early voters, while there were thousands of
vote-by-mail ballots that had been sent out, which required a number of manual and detailed processes. She stated
that she had not received complaints from residents regarding the reduced hours in the past.
Councilor Kimberley asked how many steps were involved in processing a vote by mail application. Grace
Poirier stated that there were twelve manual steps per ballot, from receipt of the application to tabulation.

Councilor Kimberley asked if the reduction in hours could deter a resident from voting. Grace Poirier stated
that it could but there were many opportunities to vote, such as vote-by-mail, two early voting Saturdays, a full
week before the election, and election day. 
Councilor Kimberley asked if volunteers were important for working the polls. Grace Poirier stated having a
good pool of election workers was very important. She stated election workers went through training and were
made sure to be up to the task.
Councilor Gross asked for clarification regarding the Saturday voting hours. Grace Poirier stated that both
Saturdays voting would be open for six hours.
Councilor Gross stated that if a resident could not make it to the polls on election day for a legitimate reason,
such as travel or a medical reason, then they were allowed to vote absentee at any time.
Councilor Grace asked for clarification regarding the reduced hours. Grace Poirier stated that the hours during
the first week would be reduced but not eliminated. 
Councilor Benson stated that he understood the amount of work the Clerk’s Office put into elections, but he
could not support reducing access to voting for residents.
Councilor Page stated her support for the matter.
Councilor Gross stated that the City Council did not support restricting voting access whatsoever, but the burden
on the Clerk’s Office was dramatic.

some days. Grace Poirier stated that the Council President and Vice President had allowed the office to close
